North Carolina Tar Heels.status: Transfer — arriving via Wisconsin, having previously been at Wake Forest and Maryland; treated as the default starter the guide would rather see replaced.
North Carolina Tar Heels.previous_school: Wisconsin; previously Maryland, and originally committed to Wake Forest in 2020.
North Carolina Tar Heels.career_experience: Committed to Wake Forest in 2020 and enrolled in 2021, then moved to Maryland, Wisconsin and now North Carolina. A mediocre Maryland starter two seasons ago.
North Carolina Tar Heels.previous_starts: Two last season, before a season-ending injury.
North Carolina Tar Heels.efficiency: Not addressed in guide; the guide says he did not look the part in his two starts.
North Carolina Tar Heels.competition: Live, and the guide takes a side. It weighs 6-foot-5 Miles O'Neill, a Petrino recruit at Texas A&M, and 6-foot-4 freshman Travis Burgess, a dual-threat four-star and 247's No. 9 quarterback in the class, and argues North Carolina should bet on upside rather than on Edwards. Its own preference is stated: it likes North Carolina more if O'Neill or Burgess start.
North Carolina Tar Heels.backup: Miles O'Neill (Texas A&M) and freshman Travis Burgess.
North Carolina Tar Heels.author_confidence: Low in the incumbent, explicitly higher in the alternatives. The guide reports Wisconsin was said to have paid around $1 million in NIL compensation and suggests North Carolina may have got a deal, since Edwards needed a medical waiver to be eligible and did virtually nothing.
North Carolina Tar Heels.positive_case: The alternatives carry upside — O'Neill is a Petrino recruit and Burgess a four-star rated No. 9 at the position in his class — and Bobby Petrino has been hired to run the offense.
North Carolina Tar Heels.concerns: Edwards started only two games last season, did not look the part, and suffered a season-ending injury; the guide calls him a mediocre Maryland starter two seasons ago.
North Carolina Tar Heels.scheme_fit: Coordinator Freddie Kitchens was dismissed and Bobby Petrino hired; O'Neill is described as a Petrino recruit.
North Carolina Tar Heels.supporting_cast: A retained core. Despite a mass exodus to the portal North Carolina kept its leading rusher, leading receiver and leading sack man — running back Demon June (464 yards on a team averaging 3.7 per carry, and third in receiving yards), receiver Jordan Shipp (60 catches, 671 yards), Melkart Abou-Jaoude (10.5 sacks), plus Kaleb Cost and Jaiden Patterson in the secondary. The guide reads this as Belichick and Michael Lombardi identifying who to pay to stay and who to pay to come.
North Carolina Tar Heels.portal_context: Edwards and O'Neill both arrived through the portal amid a mass exodus. The guide notes North Carolina signed the 19th-ranked recruiting class with over 40 recruits, and only West Virginia took more 2026 commitments.
North Carolina Tar Heels.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins, with an explicit quarterback preference attached: the guide likes North Carolina more if O'Neill or Burgess start over Edwards. The schedule is rough — an overseas opener in Dublin against TCU, a road game at Clemson, Miami, Louisville and Notre Dame at home, and two September byes — and it is candid that upsets are needed. Projection is 4.81 wins.
North Carolina Tar Heels.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide conditions how much it likes the team on which quarterback starts.
North Carolina Tar Heels.conflicts: The guide treats Edwards as the default starter while arguing the programme should start someone else; it does not resolve which will happen.

Pittsburgh Panthers.status: Returning starter — the guide says he has the job outright because Eli Holstein is at Virginia.
Pittsburgh Panthers.career_experience: Solid as a true freshman across nine starts.
Pittsburgh Panthers.passing: Not addressed in guide as a season line.
Pittsburgh Panthers.turnovers: Not addressed in guide for Heintschel individually.
Pittsburgh Panthers.competition: None — the guide states he has the job outright.
Pittsburgh Panthers.author_confidence: Positive on clarity rather than on ceiling. The guide's phrase is that there is more clarity now, and it calls him solid as a true freshman.
Pittsburgh Panthers.positive_case: Solid true-freshman production across nine starts, with the job settled and Pat Narduzzi's defensive record behind him — the guide sees a friendly schedule potentially putting Pitt on the playoff radar.
Pittsburgh Panthers.concerns: He must build rapport with many new receivers, and the guide pushes back hard on the offense he inherits: 20th in points per game while ranking 67th in yards per play, 120th in third-down conversion rate, 44 sacks allowed — fifth-most nationally — and just 3.5 yards per carry.
Pittsburgh Panthers.scheme_fit: The guide allows year three of the Kade Bell offense may improve things.
Pittsburgh Panthers.supporting_cast: The guide's main worry. It pushes back directly on other previews talking up the line's experience, observing that the experience in question is in letting defenders reach the quarterback — 87 sacks allowed over two seasons. Heintschel gets new blind-side protection from Penn transfer Netinho Olivieri, but many contributors to the 44 sacks and the 3.5 yards per carry, 119th nationally, are back.
Pittsburgh Panthers.portal_context: Eli Holstein left for Virginia, which is what settles the position; Netinho Olivieri arrives from Penn.
Pittsburgh Panthers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins. The guide concedes the schedule is genuinely favorable — which is why the Over carries the vig it does — with Pitt avoiding Clemson, SMU and Notre Dame, then counters that Virginia Tech, North Carolina and Florida State should all be markedly better. Structural schedule detail seals the case: a late bye with many new faces, five of the last eight on the road, and a season-ending trip to Berkeley. Projection is 7.43 wins.
Pittsburgh Panthers.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide's scepticism is aimed at the offense's underlying metrics and at special teams regression rather than at the quarterback specifically.
Pittsburgh Panthers.conflicts: The guide is unusually candid that it does not know what to make of Pitt's scoring output relative to its underlying metrics, attributing much of it to special teams. It leaves that unresolved.

SMU Mustangs.status: Returning starter — a senior out of eligibility after this season barring injury and a waiver.
SMU Mustangs.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
SMU Mustangs.passing: A 26-to-13 touchdown-to-interception ratio; well over 800 dropbacks across two seasons.
SMU Mustangs.rushing: Did virtually nothing as a runner last season, which the guide identifies as the biggest year-over-year change — he was never prolific, but had 300 more rushing yards in 2024. Across two seasons, 171 carries that turned potential negatives into neutral or slightly positive plays.
SMU Mustangs.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate; the guide notes only 33 sacks taken on well over 800 dropbacks.
SMU Mustangs.turnovers: Double-digit interceptions in each of the last two seasons, 13 last year.
SMU Mustangs.competition: None described — Jennings is the settled starter.
SMU Mustangs.author_confidence: Steady. The guide does not expect much regression from SMU given consistent metrics across three seasons, while naming the loss of Jennings' rushing as the biggest year-over-year change.
SMU Mustangs.positive_case: A 26-to-13 ratio and excellent sack avoidance — only 33 sacks taken on well over 800 dropbacks — which the guide says he manages well despite ball-security issues.
SMU Mustangs.concerns: Double-digit interceptions in consecutive seasons, and a rushing contribution that has all but disappeared, which the guide says must be offset elsewhere.
SMU Mustangs.scheme_fit: Lashlee calls his own plays but lost right-hand man Casey Woods to the Missouri State head job; the guide notes wryly that D'Eriq King is now a co-coordinator.
SMU Mustangs.supporting_cast: Heavily rebuilt. Jennings loses his top two receivers by yardage and four of the top five, plus leading rushers TJ Harden and Chris Johnson. SMU added running back Kendrick Raphael, now at his third ACC school, with help at receiver and tight end.
SMU Mustangs.portal_context: Kendrick Raphael arrives at running back. Per 247Sports SMU brought in only the sixth-ranked portal class among 17 ACC teams with many needs at impact positions.
SMU Mustangs.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins, with the guide explicit that it does not expect much regression. Its expectation is a season similar to last year's 8-4 regular season plus a Holiday Bowl win. Projection is 8.66 wins. The guide also introduces sack differential as a metric some handicappers it respects treat as a major tenet, noting SMU was +16 last season, down from +25 and +31.
SMU Mustangs.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide's stated separator for SMU under Lashlee is the defense, not the quarterback, though it flags the loss of Jennings' rushing as the biggest offensive change.

Stanford Cardinal.status: Transfer — from Michigan; returning from a torn ACL that cost him last season.
Stanford Cardinal.career_experience: Missed last season with a torn ACL.
Stanford Cardinal.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Stanford Cardinal.rushing: Not addressed in guide as production; the guide notes all three quarterback options are more mobile than their predecessors.
Stanford Cardinal.turnovers: Nine interceptions against seven touchdowns at Michigan — part of a programme-wide problem the guide traces at length.
Stanford Cardinal.competition: Live. UCF transfer Dylan Rizk is an option, as is true freshman Mike Mitchell, originally a Vanderbilt commit.
Stanford Cardinal.backup: UCF transfer Dylan Rizk and true freshman Mike Mitchell.
Stanford Cardinal.author_confidence: Low on the players, cautiously positive on the coach. The guide's note of optimism is explicitly about the coach rather than the players: Pritchard has worked with Jayden Daniels over recent seasons and spent five years as Commanders coordinator, so he may get something from one of them.
Stanford Cardinal.positive_case: A head coach with genuine quarterback pedigree, and three options all more mobile than their predecessors.
Stanford Cardinal.concerns: Ball security above all. The guide anchors this in a long trend: Stanford was +2 in turnover margin across the six-game 2020 season and is -33 over the five years since. Ben Gulbranson, who took most of the passing reps last year, had more interceptions than touchdowns at 10 to 9, with the team at 14 to 12 overall — and Warren's own Michigan ratio was 7 to 9.
Stanford Cardinal.supporting_cast: The line is the focus. First-time coordinator Terry Heffernan has spent much of his career coaching offensive lines, which the guide calls a good thing here. It lays out five years of sack figures — 31, 41, 41, 39 and 41 allowed against 15, 23, 23, 26 and 23 generated — and concludes that being -83 over five seasons certainly has not helped.
Stanford Cardinal.portal_context: Warren from Michigan and Rizk from UCF. A structural constraint is identified: high academic requirements make the portal far less of a shopping spree than at other schools, which the guide expects to hold the programme back again — despite a $50 million NIL collective donation.
Stanford Cardinal.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 3.5 wins. The guide acknowledges last year's team was pretty awful in many ways and still reached four wins after an 0-2 start, then provides the evidence for regression: in the four 2025 wins Stanford's yardage differentials were +10, -43, -151 and -15. Its conclusion separates quality from results — the product will probably look better without translating into victories. Projection is 3.65 wins.
Stanford Cardinal.outlook_dependency: High. Turnovers are the guide's central diagnostic for Stanford, and the quarterback room is where it locates them.

Syracuse Orange.status: Returning starter — back from the season-ending injury that the guide says was the nation's most impactful.
Syracuse Orange.previous_school: Notre Dame — he had transferred in before 2025.
Syracuse Orange.career_experience: Threw only 80 passes at Notre Dame, albeit with a 10-to-1 ratio and 72.5% completions, then produced over 1,300 yards in four starts for Syracuse before the injury.
Syracuse Orange.passing: Over 1,300 yards in four Syracuse starts with a 10-to-2 touchdown-to-interception ratio; at Notre Dame, 80 passes at 72.5% with a 10-to-1 ratio.
Syracuse Orange.turnovers: Two interceptions in his Syracuse starts; his replacements went 7 to 13.
Syracuse Orange.competition: Not described as live, but the guide names fallbacks: Amari Odom started at Kennesaw State and Malachi Nelson is on his fourth team after being a top recruit.
Syracuse Orange.backup: Amari Odom (Kennesaw State) and Malachi Nelson.
Syracuse Orange.author_confidence: Genuinely open in both directions, and the guide says so. It notes he was a three-star freshman in 2022 and a three-star transfer in 2025 per 247Sports, so he may simply have been thriving in his first real chance to start.
Syracuse Orange.positive_case: Syracuse were 3-1 and had beaten Clemson as a 17-point underdog with Angeli playing, and the split with his replacements is stark: 10-to-2 against 7-to-13, with the Orange losing eight straight by 35, 13, 17, 25, 17, 28, 63 and 22 points after he went down.
Syracuse Orange.concerns: A small career sample, and an entirely new receiver group — the top returnee having caught eight passes.
Syracuse Orange.scheme_fit: Explicitly good — the guide says he thrived in Jeff Nixon's system.
Syracuse Orange.supporting_cast: Thin at receiver: the top returning pass-catcher caught eight passes.
Syracuse Orange.portal_context: Angeli arrived from Notre Dame before 2025; Odom and Nelson are the alternatives.
Syracuse Orange.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins, with the schedule the main thing to hold against them. The offsetting factors are travel and venue — no long road trips, all six road games in the Eastern time zone, and the toughest games on paper against Louisville, SMU, Clemson and Notre Dame all at home. Despite expecting Syracuse to be an underdog often, the guide calls this one of its favorite ACC win-total bets, even with a projection of just 4.68 wins.
Syracuse Orange.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide's entire case is built on the difference Angeli's presence made, quantified through the before-and-after split.

Virginia Cavaliers.status: New starter, identity undetermined — Chandler Morris has departed and the guide names two transfer arrivals without stating which starts.
Virginia Cavaliers.previous_school: Beau Pribula arrives via Penn State and Missouri; Eli Holstein from Pitt.
Virginia Cavaliers.career_experience: Not addressed in guide for either arrival.
Virginia Cavaliers.passing: Not addressed in guide for either arrival. The departing starter, Chandler Morris, threw for 3,000 yards with a 16-to-9 ratio.
Virginia Cavaliers.competition: Unresolved in the guide. It records that the rebuild brings Penn State and Missouri transfer Beau Pribula plus Pitt transfer Eli Holstein at quarterback, without naming a starter. The Pittsburgh spread (pp. 100–101) separately confirms Holstein is at Virginia.
Virginia Cavaliers.backup: The two named arrivals are Beau Pribula and Eli Holstein; the guide does not rank them.
Virginia Cavaliers.author_confidence: Not expressed for either quarterback individually; the guide's concern is that virtually everyone on offense apart from the line is new.
Virginia Cavaliers.positive_case: Not addressed in guide at quarterback. The guide's positive case is the offensive line, which cut sacks allowed from 47 to 18 and raised yards per carry from 3.7 to 4.6, and remains mostly intact.
Virginia Cavaliers.concerns: Heavy skill-position losses: Chandler Morris after 3,000 yards and a 16-to-9 ratio, and more importantly J'Mari Taylor, who ran for over 1,000 yards with 14 touchdowns and was fourth in receptions and receiving yards, with everyone ahead of him also gone.
Virginia Cavaliers.supporting_cast: Line strong and intact; skill positions rebuilt through the portal, with running back Peyton Lewis and receiver Da'Shawn Martin named. 247Sports ranks Virginia's portal class eighth in the ACC.
Virginia Cavaliers.portal_context: Pribula, Holstein, Lewis and Martin all arrived through the portal in a class ranked eighth in the ACC by 247Sports.
Virginia Cavaliers.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins, though the guide states openly this is not a bet it would make, only a pick for the guide. It makes the call conditional on views of other teams — North Carolina, Virginia Tech, Syracuse and Florida State — because Virginia again avoids Clemson and Miami while playing at SMU and meeting West Virginia in Charlotte. Its conclusion is that 8-4 is the most likely outcome but feels closer to the ceiling. Projection is 7.79 wins.
Virginia Cavaliers.outlook_dependency: High but unattributed. The guide names the near-total turnover of the skill positions, quarterback included, as the major concern, without tying its number to a named quarterback.
Virginia Cavaliers.conflicts: The guide names two portal quarterbacks and declines to state which starts, so this record carries no VSiN preseason expectation for the position.

Virginia Tech Hokies.status: Transfer — from Penn State, following James Franklin.
Virginia Tech Hokies.career_experience: Started seven games for Penn State.
Virginia Tech Hokies.competition: Not described as live, but the guide notes Virginia Tech also brought in North Carolina quarterback Bryce Baker in the same portal class.
Virginia Tech Hokies.author_confidence: Positive and specific. The guide notes Grunkemeyer has chemistry with new tight end Luke Reynolds, and rates the portal class fourth-best in the conference.
Virginia Tech Hokies.positive_case: Seven Penn State starts, pre-existing chemistry with tight end Luke Reynolds, and a receiver addition in Que'Sean Brown, who had over 1,200 yards at Duke at 5-foot-8.
Virginia Tech Hokies.concerns: Not addressed as a quarterback concern.
Virginia Tech Hokies.scheme_fit: Continuity with the head coach and several Penn State players who followed Franklin.
Virginia Tech Hokies.supporting_cast: Improved and well-directed. Marcellous Hawkins averaged over six yards per carry and should feature more without a running quarterback like Kyron Drones. The guide adds useful context: the offense managed only 21.4 points per game but 4.9 yards per carry even with Drones dragging the average down, so Franklin could focus on skill positions rather than rebuilding the line.
Virginia Tech Hokies.portal_context: Per 247Sports Virginia Tech brought in the conference's fourth-ranked portal class, including Grunkemeyer, Bryce Baker and Que'Sean Brown; several Penn State players followed Franklin.
Virginia Tech Hokies.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 6.5 wins. The guide flags the price as somewhat expensive while calling a 5-0 start before the trip to Cal very much on the table, and its sharpest argument is comparative: Franklin does not often lose games he should win, something that trips up nearly every other ACC programme. Projection is 7.1 wins.
Virginia Tech Hokies.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide's Over rests principally on Franklin's record as a favorite and on raised talent across the roster, with the quarterback one part of a broad upgrade.

Wake Forest Demon Deacons.career_experience: A 10-to-5 touchdown-to-interception ratio at nearby North Carolina.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.passing: A 10-to-5 touchdown-to-interception ratio at North Carolina.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.rushing: Not addressed in guide as production; the guide's point is that the left-handed Lopez is not the mobile type his predecessor was.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.competition: None described — Lopez is presented as the starter.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.author_confidence: Low, and stated directly: the guide judges him a very underwhelming addition for co-coordinators Rob Ezell and Dan Enos.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.positive_case: Not addressed in guide — the guide offers no positive case for the addition.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.concerns: A specific causal chain. Robby Ashford's mobility meant Wake Forest allowed only 17 sacks after surrendering 91 across the two prior seasons and at least 35 in each of the last four; Lopez is not that type of player and the line is rebuilt. The guide asks directly whether Wake Forest should have aimed higher at the position.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.scheme_fit: Co-coordinators Rob Ezell and Dan Enos inherit him; the guide does not describe a positive fit.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.supporting_cast: Almost nothing. The offense is basically brand new apart from leading receiver Carlos Hernandez, and the offensive line is rebuilt.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.portal_context: Lopez arrives from North Carolina; Ashford and Deshawn Purdie depart. The guide cites one of the conference's worst portal hauls as a reason a downturn should be expected, while noting Wake Forest has been fundraising well for its NIL budget — and loops back to ask why, having evidently not had to spend heavily to keep the defense together, it did not aim higher on offense.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins. The guide separates its view of the coach from its view of the season, saying it rated Dickert at Washington State and still does, describes a lot of red flags blowing violently, and acknowledges the market has accounted for them in the number. Projection is 6.01 wins.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.outlook_dependency: Very high. The quarterback downgrade is the guide's first named red flag, and it links it mechanically to sacks allowed.
